title: Detection evidence
scope_note: Reduced scope. The planned chart of smoke sizes against dust sizes cannot be built: the dust experiment (DAFT) recorded only total dust number and mass, not sizes, and its dust is Arizona Road Dust. This page shows what the files do support: smoke size distributions, smoke sizes per test run, one like-for-like size comparison of smoke and dust, and a simulation of what gravity does to smoke. See ADR-0007.

gaps.text: No lunar dust or lunar dust simulant data exists in these PSI files. The only dust measured (DAFT) is Arizona Road Dust. So "could lunar dust fool a smoke detector?" is an open question here, not an answered one.
DAFT measured the total number and the total mass of dust particles, not their sizes. With no dust size distribution, smoke and dust sizes cannot be compared bin by bin, so no overlap is computed.
We have no cited source for which particle sizes ionization and light-scattering smoke detectors respond to, so the page does not show detector size ranges.

The SAME-R results workbook lists smoke detector and ionization chamber voltages per run. One column is empty, one is all zero, and the offsets and baselines are not explained, so these signals are not shown.

Different methods give different sizes for the same smoke, so they are never mixed in one series. Example: cotton lamp wick run 54 is 192 nm on microscope images and 72 nm from instrument totals. The cause was not investigated.
Microscope size distributions are available here for one run each of Kapton, cotton lamp wick and silicone. Pyrell and Teflon have per-run instrument totals only.
The unit of the PSI-115 values could not be confirmed. Each simulated curve is shown as a share of its own count; totals are not compared.

The PSI-115 model uses a stand-in smoke (dibutyl phthalate), not the SAME-R materials, and its particles are several micrometres across, much larger than most SAME-R smoke. It is shown on its own chart.
Which DAFT instrument log belongs to which dust bag is not confirmed. Only the per-bag averages from the DAFT summary workbook are used.
No SAME (PSI-102) measurement files are in this repository; only its 8-row sample list is used, in the catalog.

tem_image_diameter.label: Size on microscope images
tem_image_diameter.note: Smoke was collected on small grids and photographed with an electron microscope (TEM). Each particle was measured on the images and counted into size bins.

moment_geometric_mean.label: Middle size from instrument totals
moment_geometric_mean.note: Worked out by the SAME-R team from three instrument totals (particle number, an ionization chamber signal and particle mass), assuming a lognormal size spread. No particles were sized one by one.

diameter_of_average_mass.label: Diameter of average mass
diameter_of_average_mass.note: The size of a ball that has the average particle mass: total mass divided by total number. It needs a material density.

simulation_node_diameter.label: Size class in the simulation
simulation_node_diameter.note: The PSI-115 computer model sorts particles into 44 size classes; this is the size of each class.

smoke_bins.label: Cotton lamp wick smoke, run 54: all particles counted
smoke_bins.note: Share of counted particles in each size bin, from microscope images of one test run. This version keeps every particle, including a group of very small ones.

smoke_runs.note: One dot per test run. Test conditions (heating, air flow, aging time) differ between runs. Aged runs measured the same smoke again after it had been held for a while.

points.description: Mid Temp aging run mid high

average_mass_comparison.note: Both groups use the same size measure: total particle mass divided by total particle number, turned into the size of one ball. It is one number per test, not a size distribution, so it cannot show how much smoke and dust sizes overlap.

dust.label: Arizona Road Dust (DAFT)
dust.material_text: Arizona Road Dust (ARD Fine) in combination with ISS GN2 to create an aerosol for measurement purposes.
dust.density_note: The dust size assumes a density of 1 g/cm3 (water), as the DAFT workbook does (cell D20). Mineral dust is denser, so its real size is smaller than shown. The density of this dust is not in these files [verify].
